headers.title: Headers and constants
headers.text: The site as Referer on every picture, and the selectors and list paths the builder derived (each has its reason in the builder's card); the title page's own fields tapped in Build by tapping (Cover, Description, Tags, Author, Status; empty when not tapped); the rows tapped as Tags groups (TAG_GROUPS: name, selector, target; empty list when none); the sections tapped as Suggestions (SUGGESTION_GROUPS: name, card, link, title, cover; empty list when none); the Popular / Latest button names, tabs, filters and settings from "Lists and options" (empty lists when none were recorded).

getPopular.title: Popular
getPopular.text: The popular list path with {page} filled, one ITEM card per title: TITLE for the name and link, COVER for the picture through COVER_ATTR.

getLatest.title: Latest
getLatest.text: The latest list path, the same cards (the popular path again when the site has no separate list).

search.title: Search
search.text: The list a filter search browses and the filters' values. Each filter has a role: a page filter picks the list (the built-in “List” first in the sheet: Popular, Latest — the default — and the tabs; a menu's links such as Types → /en/censored or Trending → /en/all?sort=week; a directory's text box → /en/makers/{value}); only the first page filter changed from its default applies (the others are logged). Extra filters (type, year, sort… learned with their real codes) add param=value to whichever list is chosen, only when changed from their default, so a list keeps its own order otherwise. The page number follows the list paths' style (?page=N, /page/N or /N). With words typed: the search address with the words, plus the extras seen working on the search page; page filters and the other extras are left out with a log line. Filters written before r105 keep working: a “path” filter is a page filter, a “param” filter an extra of the search page (with no list picked it opens the search page, as before); two “path” filters of one page's parameters still combine. A grouped tag tapped on a title page arrives as “Group: tag”: a filter named like the group with an option labelled like the tag picks that option; else only the tag's words are searched. A text box with suggestions sends the names typed: each matched to its list's entry (any case), a name not in the list as a slug (logged). A filter search with 0 titles logs the address it tried.

getDetails.title: Title page
getDetails.text: The Cover, Description, Tags, Author and Status tapped on the title page first. Rows tapped as Tags groups (Cast, Maker, Genres…) give tags "Group: value" that the app shows grouped (the other tags are then "Tags: value"), and rows set to Description a "Group: a, b" line under the description. The other rows of the same details block (a "Genres" row the title you tapped didn't have) come too: links / chips as "Genres: Solowork" tags, a short plain row as a line under the description (each new row is logged once). Else og:image, a video poster or the player's poster as cover, and no cover at all when the page has none, so the list's cover stays; og:description unless it is the site's own slogan (the home page's description, read once); genre / tag links outside the site's menus (nav, header, footer, aside, menus), without words like "Genres" or "Tags". Author and status only when tapped. A field whose selector fails is logged (Logs) and read as empty, so the others still come.

getChapterList.title: Chapters / episodes
getChapterList.text: The CHAPTER links of the title page, each address once, the last number in the text as the number, the picked date element when there is one. When the title page is the only episode (SINGLE_EPISODE), that page is episode 1 with the picked date / number read on it. With no chapter link picked the part is not written, and a JSON build is written as JS (the JSON format can't say why there are no chapters; the JS one throws "No chapter link was picked…"). The only episode gets the title's picture as its thumbnail (the Cover tapped on the title page, else og:image, a video poster or twitter:image).

getPageList.title: Pages
getPageList.text: The IMAGE pictures of the chapter page, the address from IMAGE_ATTR then the lazy-load attributes and src.

getVideoList.title: Videos
getVideoList.text: The app's video finder (host.findVideo) opens the episode page in the hidden browser, presses Play and catches the stream the player asks for (.m3u8 / .mpd / .mp4), also when the site's script fills in the player's address; then it opens the player itself with the page as Referer. HLS is split into qualities; the quality / server settings put the preferred ones first. Nothing caught: the error says why (no player, never asked for a video, streams in pieces, page didn't load).

extras.title: Tabs, filters and settings
extras.text: Added only when "Lists and options" recorded some: tabs become buttons at the top of Browse (getCatalogs / getCatalog with the same cards), filters the filter sheet: the built-in “List” first, then dropdowns, sort lists, checkboxes, text and text boxes with suggestions, each with its role (page / extra); filters with a group name sit under that heading. Settings become the source's settings (read with host.preference.get("key")). Sections tapped as Suggestions add getRelated: each section's cards on the title page (link, name, picture without placeholders), returned as named groups; a section the site's script fills in after the page loads is read from the address it really comes from (the title's address parts filled in), or with the hidden browser when that was chosen (slower, waits for the cards); a section's Load more button can be pressed up to 3 times (the next pages from the address one press asks for, else pressed in the hidden browser).

helpers.title: Helpers
helpers.text: One request with the site as Referer, the list path with {page} / {q} filled, the value a filter sends, the filters as search uses them (the built-in List first, each filter's role), a page filter's address with the page number in the list paths' style, a parameter set in an address, picture addresses without data: or placeholder images, a late section's address and reply, a section read in the hidden browser (its Load more pressed there), the shared card parser (titles with a hidden word left out when the source has that setting), absolute addresses and the last number of a text.

3.note: Videos use the app's video finder: plays players whose address the site's script fills in and catches DASH.

4.note: Title page: the cover / description / tags / author you tap; keeps the list cover when the page has none; skips the site-wide description and menu links.

5.note: Tags grouped by the rows you tap (Cast, Maker…); tapping a grouped tag searches it in the source.

6.note: Filters made from the site's menus: one per group; long lists can be a text box with suggestions.

7.note: Suggestions from the title page's sections (You may like, Related); filters that open their own page (Trending) are used only when one is picked (an empty “Any” first), each filter goes only into its own page's address; the only episode gets the title's picture; the title page's readers log their errors.

8.note: Filters have a role: page filters pick the list (a “List” filter first: Popular, Latest, tabs), extra filters (type, year, sort…) add their code to whichever list is chosen; filters can sit in groups; suggestion covers skip placeholders; a suggestions section the site loads later is read from its own address. Dropdowns and sorts start with an empty “Site default”, so the site’s own first option can be picked; a filter search stays on the list Browse was showing (Popular, Latest or a tab) unless List is changed; another list gets its page number as /N unless the lists use a page word (/page/N); a directory slug read with %XX isn’t encoded twice; covers named pixel-… or lazy-… and Cloudinary addresses (w_200,h_300) are kept, one picture on every card is skipped.

9.note: Suggestions: a section the site loads later can be read with the browser (the title page in the hidden browser, waiting for its cards); a section's “Load more” can be pressed up to 3 times (the next pages from the address one press asks for, else pressed in the hidden browser). Each section is its own named row on the title screen, for anime and manga.

10.note: Collections: a directory (genres, makers, people, series…) is a collection filter whose entries keep their parts apart (number, name, videos, views, likes, picture; never a Follow button), with the site's own sort options and menus; a live collection is read page by page as Browse scrolls (getDirectory). The built-in “List” filter stays in getFilters (the app hides it; the Browse tabs pick the list). Suggestions: a section that fails no longer fails the others, each section's outcome is logged, and the hidden browser gets 35 s at most for all sections.

11.note: Collections: getDirectory also serves collections kept in the source (Browse reads the site's pages when its own sort or a menu such as Height, Cup or Age is picked); a sort's first option can be the site's default under its own name (“Most videos”), never “Site default”. Pictures: when a card's img has no address or a placeholder, its lazy-load attributes, a <picture>'s <source>, a background-image or data-bg, or an img inside <noscript> are read (suggestions, list covers, collection faces).

12.note: A collection entry's part that can't be read (its selector fails) is now logged once in the console instead of being skipped silently, so Lint no longer flags “a catch that swallows the error” in sources made from this template.

13.note: Title page: the details block's rows that no Tags group lists (a “Genres” row the title you built from didn't have) are read too: links / chips as “Genres: Solowork” tags, a short plain row as a line under the description. Works from the groups you already have, no re-tapping.
